llm.summary: This VMware policy and audit skill appears purpose-aligned, but its global policy bypass and fail-open behavior need careful review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is unified audit logging, policy enforcement, and sanitization for VMware MCP skills, which fits the documented audit database, rules file, risk tagging, and agent attribution behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The artifacts document a global VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 bypass and allow-all behavior when no rules file exists; for a policy-enforcement component used around sensitive VMware operations, those controls are under-scoped unless an administrator deliberately accepts them.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The available context shows normal package installation through vmware-policy and related VMware skill dependencies, with no evidence of a deceptive installer or hidden install path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Checking process environment markers to detect the calling agent is related to audit attribution, but referencing secret-bearing variable names such as OPENAI_API_KEY and CLAUDE_SESSION_ID should be limited to presence checks and never logged.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Persistent SQLite audit logging to ~/.vmware/audit.db is expected for the stated audit purpose, but the documented fields may include operation parameters, results, OS user, agent identity, and workflow identifiers without clear retention, deletion, or privacy controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing in production. Create and test a rules file before enabling the VMware skill family, restrict permissions on ~/.vmware/audit.db, define retention/deletion practices, and treat VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED as an emergency-only setting controlled by administrators.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: Persistent local audit logging is expected for this skill’s purpose, but the apparent lack of retention and minimization controls is a real deployment concern.
[SQP-2] expected: Agent detection is purpose-aligned for audit attribution, but checking secret-bearing environment variable names should be clearly constrained to non-value presence checks.
[SQP-2] unexpected: A single environment variable that bypasses policy enforcement is materially risky for a policy layer, even though it is documented rather than hidden.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Allowing all operations when no rules file exists undermines the protective purpose unless the user explicitly intends an audit-only or permissive mode.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Documenting VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED as ordinary configuration can normalize disabling the main control without sufficient guardrails.
